bluf: Firegang is a Spokane, WA dental marketing company selling websites, PPC, SEO, Facebook ads, reviews and AI search to practices, fronted by a practice growth self assessment and a claim to be the #1 dental marketing company. Its record shows a house gone quiet: 41 Google video ads last shown 2026-01-29 with 0 in the last 30 days, 0 sitemap URLs updated in 365 days, and 3 clients who are names only. The one thing a rival should know: the Horus read is Exposed at -17.7, most exposed to KJ4, and the Monsoon read is Landfall at 75.8, so its book very likely buys on price.
doing:
Firegang positions itself as a full service dental marketing company promising practice growth through websites, PPC, SEO, Facebook ads, reviews and AI search, fronted by a practice growth self assessment: in plain words, one supplier for everything a dental practice buys, sold through a diagnostic that sorts dentists into a green zone or a red zone. Its headline claim is that it is the #1 dental marketing company, citing $2M+ collections growth and doubled new patients for clients, and its homepage bills the team as best selling dental marketing authors and an award winning company.

The mix is nine services, every one prefixed Dental. Three lines lead at a score of 3: Paid Search (the meta sells expert PPC, Dental PPC in the nav), SEO (expert SEO in the meta, Dental SEO in the What We Do list) and Web & Product (the meta leads with stunning web design, Dental Websites heads the list). Two core lines score 2: Local (reputation management, an Online Reviews block, JSON-LD pitching multi location scaling) and Paid Social (Dental Facebook Ads). The one proprietary product is the Dental Practice Growth Self-Assessment; no partner is listed.

Its AI posture is a label: Dental AI Search Optimization is listed first in the services menu, and no AI search copy, tools or automation was captured beyond it, so AI Search / GEO scores 1 and AI Automation / Agents 0.

The record lists no dated moves, news or jobs. Pricing signals are a free 2 minute self assessment and a free practice growth call; no prices were captured and the Horus read marks the pricing model unknown. Conspicuously absent for a practice growth shop: Data & Measurement and Email & CRM both score 0, Content & Digital PR scores 1, ownership is unknown, and no case study describes the work behind any client.
clients:
The record marks its client type as SMB, lists one vertical, dental, and one office, Spokane, WA, so the home market is US dental practices.

The book holds 3 clients and all 3 are names only, with 0 observed needs: Centro Dental Las Americas and Evergreen Smile Studio come from homepage testimonials, and Dr. Ben Hill, described in the record as a Spokane area family dental practice, comes from a homepage case study. None of the three carries a described result or a service named, so each need is inferred from what it leads with rather than observed: web build and platform, paid performance and organic demand, with local lead generation behind them, because Dental Websites, Dental PPC and Dental SEO head its own menu. The record does not say which of those any of the three came for.

No client on record sits on another tracked agency's book, and the record names no overlap.

What the base needs next is a judgment tied to the edition. The read is most exposed to KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer), driven by Paid Search and Paid Social, and to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that the PPC and Facebook ads hours these practices buy are the first to be absorbed by platform automation, and that what they need next is local lead generation measured in calls and bookings, the LSA and Sponsored Places work under P3 that the record shows Firegang does not do. The tailwind is KJ2 (ads inside AI answers), which a dental practice buys only with proof, and the record holds no proof yet; the evidence for all of this is thin, which is a question to put to its clients.
house: The record marks 1 of 2 scored say and do lines practised. Paid Search is corroborated: it runs its own Google ads, 41 in the Transparency Center, 0 in the last 30 days. Paid Social is unknown: no pixel detected. LinkedIn advertising is contradicted, the one gap listed: it sells paid social or B2B demand gen and runs no LinkedIn ads. Publishing cadence was not measured, though the sitemap lists 270 URLs with 0 updated in 90 days and 0 in 365, read by the openings as idle; the llms.txt check is unrecorded, no AI crawlers are blocked and 0 AI URLs were found. The tag stack is gtm and ga4 on WordPress, with no social pixel, test tool or ABM stack. Its Google Ads Transparency Center record shows 41 ads under Firegang Inc, all video, last shown 2026-01-29. Its LinkedIn record shows 0 ads. No Meta or TikTok check is recorded.
market:
The Horus read puts Firegang at a tailwind index of -17.7, band Exposed, resilience 36.3. It is best placed for KJ2 at net 0.219 on Paid Search and AI Search / GEO, and for KJ1 at 0.164; it is most exposed to KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) at -0.547, driven by Paid Search and Paid Social, and to KJ6 at -0.38. The best scenario fit is The Walled Oasis at 44/100. It is partial on P1 (audited AI visibility), P3 (LSAs and Sponsored Places) and P4 (inputs for automation); P2, P6, P7 and P8 are absent; P5 is unknown, no pricing being public.

The Monsoon read is 75.8, band Landfall, migration 69.8 against displacement 81.8, inferred from the SMB ICP term. 70 of the index is the sold mix, SEO (17) and Web & Product (17) most movable; the shore split sends 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America, and automation overlaps 23% of the movable hours. No hub office or onshore claim is listed; the footprint is inferred.
openings:
The strongest opening is price. With displacement 81.8 on the Monsoon read and an SMB dental book, it is very likely, with moderate confidence since the read is inferred, that an offshore delivered rival can undercut its website and SEO hours. The falsifier is a next compile showing a public outcome priced model and case studies with described results.

The contradiction to lead with is its own advertising: it sells expert PPC and Facebook ads while its Google ads were last shown 2026-01-29 and it runs no LinkedIn ads, so a rival with live ads can show a practice the difference. The judgment exposure is KJ4: PPC and paid social hours are the ones platform automation removes, and P4 is partial, so an offer built on first party data, creative volume and measurement is likely to win.

Three gaps are unclaimed: P3 (sells local at depth, no LSA or Sponsored Places work), P1 (sells Dental AI Search Optimization with no audited product) and P5 (no public pricing), so an outcome priced local offer with an audited AI visibility number is a conversation it cannot have in public. All 3 clients are names only, each contestable on evidence of work.
